# Release update and validation record

This update starts from the original anonymous Hugging Face release. The project
owner has requested publication of the prepared package with source attribution,
without further calorimetry source-to-task reconstruction work. CADD and ESM
payloads are excluded in favor of tested direct upstream downloads. Statements
below describe validation scope, not blanket redistribution permission.

- Stage the inputs necessary to evaluate the prepared benchmark, including physics.
- Link upstream construction datasets rather than copying complete collections.
- Use one model index and model-neutral reporting directory. `results/new_models`
  remains a compatibility symlink only; historical ledger filenames are provenance.
- Preserve original manifests, adjudications, grades and score tables byte-for-byte.
  Identity-only edits to recorded traces are explicitly logged and checked for
  unchanged JSON structure and non-string values.
- Add Fable artifacts under the same run layout, retaining refusal and coverage
  distinctions. Fallback replay remains separate from actually evaluated models.
- Restore the shared task loader and L3 runner. Relocate archived paths in memory,
  without editing historical manifests or scoring evidence.

`VALIDATION.md` describes the original snapshot, not execution validation of this
update. `MANIFEST.sha256` is refreshed for the current release; runtime checksums
are in `verification/runtime_files.csv`. Preservation checks are generated by
`python update_release_metadata.py`, allowing only ledger-verified trace identity
redactions in previously published evidence files.

Remaining publication gates are in `RUNTIME_DATA.md`. Current result reproduction
is described below; this is not a claim that every illustrative figure or appendix
artifact has been rebuilt.
No benchmark model was rerun, no paper was edited, and no history was rewritten.

## Repository anonymity cleanup

`clean_release_identity.py` removes account identifiers from text, normalizes tar
ownership, and redacts BAM program-history headers. It verifies archive member
payloads and BAM alignment records/reference sequences remain identical, then
rebuilds BAM indexes. Original files are backed up outside the release directory.
The cleanup ledger contains hashes and invariants, never the removed identities.

`audit_release_identity.py` scans the release file selection and compressed
contents without executing serialized model files. `refresh_release_manifest.py`
regenerates the whole-package manifest after all checks and reports are finalized.
These checks must run after future staging, which can import fresh metadata.
Publish only this checked Git/manifest file selection, never a recursive upload
of the raw workspace. Ignored environments and caches can contain local paths.

This clone now has repository-local anonymous author/committer defaults and
automatic commit/tag signing disabled. No global Git configuration was changed.
Previously published traces contain identifiers in the base revision. That
remote history is not repaired by this cleanup and must be addressed explicitly
before presenting the repository as fully anonymous, without promising that
previous downloads can be recalled.

## Completed checks

- All ten track specs import with the same model roster.
- All manifest-selected task inputs and declared read-only resources resolve.
- Seven packaging unit tests pass (paths, reference overrides, cache overrides,
  spec loading, reporting compatibility, source-policy TSV structure, and
  literal interpreter aliases used by sealed execution).
- Original evidence/score preservation is checked against the base Git revision,
  including records now reachable through the compatibility symlink.
- Newly added text received a logged local-path anonymization pass. This is not a
  claim of exhaustive identity/credential screening.

An isolated Python 3.11 CPU environment imports the scientific dependencies,
including pyBigWig, Scanpy, PyTorch and ESM. Its observed versions are recorded in
`environment/runtime-smoke-requirements.txt`, not claimed as the historical run
environment. All 46 authority-index manifests pass representative input-loading
checks in network-disabled bubblewrap sandboxes (`verification/runtime_smoke.json`).
The probe confirms that the authority index is not visible and API-key environment
variables are not inherited. It samples one world per manifest, not every task;
it does not validate full analyses, checkpoint inference, or live model execution.

The smoke test exposed an interpreter-alias packaging issue with uv-created
environments. `sandbox_seal.py` now mounts the literal symlink-target interpreter
prefix as well as its resolved prefix. This does not expose the enclosing home or
repository directory, or change any grades, data, or scientific task settings.

MIT was approved for DISCERN-authored code. The 2026-09-25 source update identifies
Goddard's nuclear-decay measurement dataset with explicit CC BY 4.0 terms and the
specific calorimetry and CADD source records. Official Meta cards label both
required ESM-2 models MIT licensed. Calorimetry and CADD redistribution questions,
ESM file-level coverage/notice checks, and attribution of separately sourced
physics inputs remain documented in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. Source verification
does not by itself clear the entire package for publication. No data, grades,
historical manifests, or paper files were changed by this documentation update.
A verified Git bundle backs up the original
published Git history outside this repository. Its local LFS object store was
backed up separately and compared byte-for-byte. No public history rewrite,
upload, or release pin has occurred.

## Current result reproduction

### Additional pre-upload checks (2026-09-25)

Fresh upstream downloads reproduce both ESM-2 checkpoints and both contact heads
byte-for-byte and the CADD panel as identical decompressed text. The new
`fetch_external_runtime.py` supports omitting these payloads from the upload;
see `EXTERNAL_RUNTIME.md` and `verification/upstream_runtime_check.json`.
All 46 isolated input-loading probes and all seven packaging tests passed again.
Network-disabled reproduction regenerated ten leaderboard rows and Figures 3–5
without changing their source tables. These checks apply to the local candidate,
not yet to a published snapshot.

The prepared calorimetry payload remains an upload gate. The public ThermoML
catalog points to NIST's general licensing statement, but its third-party
journal-source scope still needs resolution. The L3 builder also depends on
unpackaged intermediate shadow assets, so an upstream-only reconstruction route
has not been certified. Auxiliary nuclear detector-calibration data require their
own attribution/terms check rather than inheriting Goddard's CC BY 4.0 license.
These uncertainties remain disclosed; publication does not mark them resolved.

`reproduce_current_results.py` regenerates result Figures 3–5 and the ten numeric
rows of Table 1, separately from the archived six-model table builder. The builder
ran successfully in a credential-cleared, network-disabled sandbox exposing only
the candidate repository and interpreter/system dependencies, not the private
benchmark or Overleaf tree. It verifies the 192 track-stage values, 64 clean and
568 challenged L1 evaluations, 172 eligible L3 outcomes, 94 hypotheses, and 17
plotted stability measures against the saved exports. Source input hashes remain
unchanged. A read-only numeric comparison against the current LaTeX confirms that
every Table 1 numeric cell in all ten rows matches at the displayed precision.

Fable's L2 row deliberately uses its published five-track conditional meta
summary. It must not be replaced by a mean over raw grades or all replay cells.
The replay itself remains a derived scenario, not a separately evaluated model.
Source summaries and exports are retained rather than rewritten, including their
historical rounding. No raw-transcript regrading, scientific score changes, or
paper edits were performed. Numerical agreement is not a claim of byte-identical
PDF rendering across Matplotlib/font versions.
